headline: Right-of-way proceedings started for 1720 Spear Street; site visit and hearing set for February 10th.
summary: This step stops a 120-day clock that started when the DRB denied a subdivision application for the property, filed by Green Mountain Habitat for Humanity. Staff are still negotiating with the property owners. The meeting also covered a list of state legislative priorities, and staff asked members to send their top five by Tuesday.
decisions: Approved starting right-of-way proceedings and opening a public hearing for 1720 Spear Street, unanimously.
Approved February 10th at 3:00 p.m. for the site visit and 5:00 p.m. for the hearing, unanimously.
discussion: Legislative priorities list: Members discussed how many items to send to the state delegation, with three to five suggested, and asked for a spreadsheet to review each item.
Local option tax: Members discussed a possible 2% local option tax charter change, and staff said the city cannot see detailed receipts for the tax.
Class 1 highway funding: Members discussed a formula change that would count vehicle miles traveled, noting that Williston Road is the most traveled road in the state.
Energy codes and e-motos: Members questioned whether the city can enforce energy codes, which staff is getting a legal opinion on, and some opposed limiting e-moto sales to dealers.

decision_evidence.quote: Move to I may I move to institute proceedings and open public hearing to schedule examination of premises and public hearing on necessity and compensation/damages for rights to lay out the right-of-way shown on the official city map over the property known as 1720 Spear Street. ... Aye. It is unanimous.

I move that we select February 10th at 3:00 p.m. as the date and time for the, uh, site visit to examine the premises, and the public hear and conduct the public hearing on necessity and compensation or damages. ... Aye. It's also unanimous.

decision_titles: February 10th site visit and hearing, 1720 Spear Street
